entities.summary:
hysteresis is a phenomenon in which a system fails to return to its original state after a change, leading to a persisting effect. This concept has been observed in various fields, including physics, engineering, and economics, and has significant implications for understanding complex systems and their behavior.

During the Classical era, hysteresis played a crucial role in the development of various technologies and scientific disciplines. The discovery of hysteresis in magnetic materials, for example, led to the creation of more efficient motors and generators, which in turn had a profound impact on industry and commerce.

The concept of hysteresis also influenced the work of scientists and philosophers, who sought to understand the underlying mechanisms and principles that governed its behavior. The French physicist Pierre Curie, for example, was one of the first scientists to study hysteresis in detail, and his work laid the foundation for modern research in this field.

One key figure associated with the study of hysteresis is the American physicist Louis Néel, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1970 for his work on the phenomenon. In his speech, Néel stated, 'The discovery of the hysteresis loop in ferrite materials has opened up a new field of research in magnetism.'
